chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim, (peace be upon him) said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): A man was obligated by the duty of Islam (to perform Hajj), and he intended to perform Hajj. He was told: 'Marry, then perform Hajj.' He said: 'If I marry before I perform Hajj, my slave is freed.' So he married before performing Hajj. He said: 'His slave was freed.' I said: 'He did not intend the face of Allah (Exalted) by freeing him.' He said: 'It is a vow in obedience to Allah, and Hajj is more deserving than marriage, and more obligatory upon him than marriage.' I said: 'Indeed, Hajj is voluntary (nafl).' He said: 'And even if it is voluntary, it is obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He has freed his slave.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow to free a slave if one marries before performing Hajj, according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on conditional emancipation vows (*nathr*), establishing that freeing a slave is an act of obedience (*ta'ah*) to Allah regardless of whether the primary trigger was obligatory or voluntary. The Imam emphasizes that Hajj, even when voluntary, holds precedence over marriage, thereby validating the vow's fulfillment as a valid act of worship rather than merely a contractual obligation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the spiritual merit of the act (emancipation) is preserved even if the intent behind the condition was pragmatic.
